models_evaluated: FDA-cleared commercial pulmonary embolism detection model

links.outcome: PE detection sensitivity variation by scanner manufacturer and acquisition parameters
links.effect: Decreased sensitivity for different scanner vendors (OR 0.25, 95% CI 0.14-0.46; OR 0.34, 95% CI 0.17-0.69), thicker slices (OR 0.74 per mm), and imaging artifacts (OR 0.33).
links.quote: Multivariable analysis showed significant associations between decreased sensitivity and scanner manufacturer (odds ratio [OR] 0.25, 95% CI 0.14-0.46 and OR 0.34, 95% CI 0.17-0.69, for different vendors versus reference, P < .003), increased slice thickness (OR 0.74, 95% CI 0.57-0.95 per 1-mm increase, P = .018), presence of imaging artifacts (OR 0.33, 95% CI 0.23-0.48, P < .001), heart failure (OR 0.58, 95% CI 0.38-0.88, P = .010), and pulmonary hypertension (OR 0.44, 95% CI 0.25-0.77, P = .004).

links.outcome: Real-world performance of FDA-cleared PE model versus expected performance locally
links.effect: Overall sensitivity 83.5% (95% CI 81.3%-85.5%), PPV 90.5%; performance varied with technical factors and comorbidities such as heart failure and pulmonary hypertension.
links.quote: The findings highlight the need for local validation frameworks that account for institution-specific technical infrastructure and patient populations, to ensure safe AI deployment across diverse clinical environments.

links.outcome: Model performance differences across demographic subgroups (age, gender, race, BMI)
links.effect: Age, gender, race, and body mass index showed no significant associations with model performance.
links.quote: Demographic factors including age, gender, race, and body mass index showed no significant associations with model performance.

screen.reason: Retrospective real-world validation of an FDA-cleared commercial PE detection model across 11,144 CT scans to evaluate technical and demographic factors driving performance heterogeneity, informing post-deployment monitoring.
